series.label: Federal funds rate
series.note: The effective overnight rate — the anchor for the whole US curve.

series.label: Consumer price index
series.note: The full consumer basket. Shown as a year-over-year rate, which is how anyone reads it.

series.label: Core CPI
series.note: Headline less food and energy — used because it forecasts headline better than headline does.

series.label: Core PCE price index
series.note: The Federal Reserve's preferred measure, and the one its 2% target refers to.

series.label: Unemployment rate
series.note: Lagging, politically decisive, and blind to whether a rise came from layoffs or from labour supply.

series.label: Nonfarm payrolls
series.note: Timely, noisy and revised. Read the trend, not the print.

series.label: Job openings
series.note: Falling openings without rising unemployment is the benign cooling path.

series.label: Real GDP
series.note: Quarterly, heavily revised, and still the reference series.

series.label: Industrial production
series.note: A small share of employment and an outsized share of the cycle's amplitude.

series.label: Housing starts
series.note: The most rate-sensitive sector in the economy, and therefore the first to turn.

series.label: Consumer sentiment
series.note: A weak predictor of spending and a strong predictor of politics.

series.label: Money supply (M2)
series.note: Watched closely in 2021 and much less since. Its relationship to inflation is regime-dependent.

series.label: World GDP growth
series.note: Annual. World Bank data is revised and typically lags the present by a year or more.

series.label: Population aged 65+
series.note: Annual. World Bank data is revised and typically lags the present by a year or more.

series.label: Electricity use per capita
series.note: Annual. World Bank data is revised and typically lags the present by a year or more.

series.label: Trade as share of world GDP
series.note: Annual. World Bank data is revised and typically lags the present by a year or more.
